questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold outside.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even in warm weather.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially when riding at night. Bright, reflective clothing helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances.

questions.question: To minimize fatigue on a long trip, you should:
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest, even if you do not feel tired. Most experienced riders limit themselves to six hours of riding per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tire quickly, so dress to protect yourself.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should generally be:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to allow the wind to catch the fabric.
Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to prevent you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly to prevent flapping in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic or pedestrians, and then proceed when safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are never very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to ride safely. Always ask your doctor how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you more easily.

questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. When released, the throttle should:

options.text: Snap back to its resting position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snap back to its resting position.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check that your throttle snaps back when you release it. Also check that your clutch feels tight and smooth.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: It should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Having just one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can reduce your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can reduce your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be convicted of impaired riding even if you are below the legal alcohol limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots give your feet the best protection. Choose boots that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: How fast does the human body remove alcohol?
questions.explanation: On average, the body removes about one drink per hour. This varies by person. The safest choice is never to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to think about when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane is about to end.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow traffic light warns that the signal is about to change to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Mirrors alone are not enough to see everything around you.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection. They should be high and sturdy to support your ankles.

questions.question: What should you think about first when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is most important. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and has a DOT safety rating.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, what must you do?
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your speed increases.

questions.question: Which item is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing like long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots, and leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible. A baseball cap does not provide protection.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned when sitting on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm tiredness and lets you control the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by three things: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.
